# Twenty Questions, Reversed

A Skill Harbor house build: the classic twenty questions, played both ways in a single solo game refereed by your own Muse, right in chat. In Phase A, you think of a secret subject and announce only its category, one of six: animal, object, trade, place, fictional character, or food. Your assistant then has at most 20 closed questions to find it. In Phase B the roles reverse: your assistant picks a subject in the same perimeter, seals it in writing, announces only its category, and you get at most 20 closed questions to find it. One game, two deductions, each side measured on the same bound.

Phase A is button play, with its discipline written down. The assistant asks one closed question at a time, numbered as it goes, and you answer with three buttons, always Yes, No, and I do not know. An I do not know answer counts in the 20, because the bound measures exchanges, not useful answers, and it never lets the assistant rule anything out. Naming a subject as a guess also counts as a question, and the assistant may not try a name before the 8th counted exchange, so luck cannot dress up as strategy. Between questions, the assistant keeps its journal in the game state: ruled out families with dated reasons, live leads, and any incoherence in your answers, where the first answer always stands. Its questions stick to perceptible traits and common knowledge, never encyclopedia detail.
